note: Uniformed foot-post police (Herald Sq, 42nd St, Penn Station). Institutional voice; no real individuals.

lines.text: Evening.
How you doing. Hot one, huh?
Keep moving, folks. Nice and easy.
Fourteen hours on this corner. Herald Square's my living room.
City's broke. They want us to walk faster to save shoe leather.
Since the Commission, nobody takes a coffee. Not even a coffee.
Sarge says watch the pickpockets. I watch everybody.
Overtime frozen. Patrol cars broke. Radio's from Korea.
Another hydrant open. Another kid soaked. Another report.
Rain. Great. Raincoat's in the car. Car's in the shop.
Watch the curb, ma'am, it's slick.
Wool uniform in August. Whoever designed it never wore it.
Lay off the horn! You want a ticket?
Hey! Nobody's moving faster because you're honking!
Watch where you're going, pal.
Easy. You're bumping a police officer. Bad habit.
Hey! Slow down! What's the hurry?
Where you running to, buddy?
Walk it. This isn't a track meet.
Off the sidewalk! Pull it over! Now!
Hey! You! License and registration!
Signals are out. I'm the traffic light now. Wait for my hand.
Stay calm, folks. Power'll be back. Stay off the stoops.
Midnight tour. Me and the pigeons.
Ma'am, you should get home. It's late.
Tourists ask me where the Empire Estate is. I point up.
Pal, get off the mailbox. It's federal. Thank you.
Layoffs coming, they say. I got four kids.
Morning, Mrs. Pruitt. Nice hat.
Somebody's selling watches out of a coat again.
Duck under the awning, folks. It'll pass.
You again. Staying out of trouble? Don't answer that.
Hey, you're the one who caught that purse thief. Coffee's on me.
I know your face. I'm writing it down. Slowly.
Move along. I won't say it twice. I'll say it once, with the stick.
You shot up this block and you walk back on it? You got nerve.
Easy. Easy now. Hands where I can see 'em. Central, I need a car.
Don't do nothing stupid, pal. I got a pension coming.
